subject: Urban Planning
title: Aging Infrastructure: America's D+ Report Card
description: A micro-lesson that makes Aging Infrastructure: America's D+ Report Card usable.

hook.text: The American Society of Civil Engineers gives US infrastructure a D+ grade. Bridges, pipes, and roads are crumbling.

buildup.text: 45,000 US bridges are structurally deficient. 2.2 million miles of pipeline are nearing the end of their designed lifespan.

discovery.text: Deferred maintenance saves money today but costs far more later. A $1 repair ignored now becomes a $10 emergency replacement.

twist.text: The 2021 Infrastructure Act allocated $1.2 trillion — but the total repair backlog exceeds $4.6 trillion. It's not even close.

climax.text: Other countries reinvest 5-9% of GDP in infrastructure. The US invests 2.4%. The gap shows in every pothole and pipe break.

punchline.text: We built the world's best infrastructure in the 1950s. Then we stopped maintaining it.

quiz.question: What grade does the ASCE give American infrastructure?
options: B — acceptable but needs some improvement
D+ — mostly below standard with many deficient systems
F — failing across all categories without exception
